title.narrative: Scaling up malaria prevention, control, and treatment through all sectors in Liberia - Liberia (01-Jul-2021-30-Jun-2024)

description.narrative: Liberia, Malaria, Plan International, Inc. (Plan International Liberia)This program has the following goals: By end of 2025, reduce malaria burden by 75% (11% overall prevalence) compared to 2016 (45% prevalence). The objectives of this program are: By end of 2025, reduce malaria mortality rates by at least 75% (43/100,000 population) compared to 2016 (172/100,000 population). By end of 2025, reduce malaria case incidence by at least 75% (95/1,000 population) compared to 2016 (380/1,000 population). By end of 2025, promote and maintain a culture of evidence-based decision making to achieve malaria program performance at all levels. By end of 2025, strengthen and maintain capacity for program management, coordination and partnership to achieve malaria program performance at all levels

title.narrative: Impact indicators targets and results for LBR-M-PIIP05
Malaria parasite prevalence: Proportion of children aged 6-59 months with malaria infection
In-patient malaria deaths: rate per 100,000 persons per year
Outcome indicators targets and results for LBR-M-PIIP05
Proportion of households with at least one insecticide-treated net for every two people and/or sprayed by IRS within the last 12 months
Proportion of population that slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night
Proportion of children under five years old who slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night
Proportion of population with access to an ITN within their household
Proportion of pregnant women who slept under an insecticide-treated net the previous night
Coverage / Output indicators targets and results for LBR-M-PIIP05
Proportion of pregnant women attending antenatal clinics who received three or more doses of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria
Proportion of suspected malaria cases that receive a parasitological test in the community
Percentage of service delivery reports from community health workers integrated into HMIS
Proportion of confirmed malaria cases that received first-line antimalarial treatment in the community
